### Architect · Answer

Event: `65c2d2f2b7058ed71ffbe8dbb70c2207` · 2026-09-28T02:34:36Z

> Decided: (a), in exact form. Not an owner choice: it tightens R12 and changes no wall. Return-only (c) breaks the page's own claim, "no share is gained by carving". Deferring (b) leaves the steward, which carves for every lease, over-charged.
> 
> The rule, as a new planned section docs/kernel/scheduling.md#the-lead-follows-the-weight (Status planned · M1, Open: none). What a budget owes is runtime, and every weight change, carve and return alike, keeps it exactly. After the fold at the old weight, the lead and the remainder are converted together, the same way a lift converts a child's work:
>   W = (pass - floor)+ x w_old + rem;  pass = floor + W / w_new;  rem = W mod w_new
> - A carve and its return with no run between are exact inverses: no rounding loss, so nothing to game. This replaces the remainder-only `rescale`.
> - A budget below the floor owes only its remainder, and waking would lift it to the floor anyway.
> - At a destruction, the carve returns (and the parent converts) before the lift, which already uses the parent's restored weight.
> 
> Other edits (unstaged):
> - The fold bullet points to the new section.
> - "Running while carved down": its status line states the breach, on the I14 model (remainder-only today, over-charging the budget that carved).
> - The "Carving while running over-charges" residual is gone, and so is "per weight change" in the rounding residual.
> - docs/todo/carve-lead-rescale.md: Why states the two-direction reason. Done when is concrete: kernel and stride `rescale` convert; model and oracle agree; a host test that carve+return leaves pass and rem unchanged; a mutation rescaling only on return fails a check; a bench case that carves while running, returns, and gets its share back against an equal victim; the pages go built and the breach goes.
> 
> Checks: mdbook build docs exit 0; cargo run -q -p redoubt-doccheck exit 0.
> 
> For K7: `a_rescale_loses_under_one_unit` should become the exact-inverse test.
